# IGNORED-TEST ROUTES — where every `#[ignore]`d test in this workspace actually runs.
#
# THE READER IS `scripts/check-ignored-test-routing.py`; read its header for the full
# argument. The short version: `#[ignore]` in this tree does not mean "broken", it means
# "a real recursion fold that takes minutes". `armed-teeth.yml` exists to run those on a
# schedule — and it decides WHICH by globbing filenames:
#
#     for f in circuit-prove/tests/*tooth*.rs circuit-prove/tests/*teeth*.rs
#
# so a tooth earns its nightly by living in a file whose NAME contains "tooth". Measured
# 2026-08-07 at HEAD, that reached 20 of the 282 `#[ignore]`d tests in the workspace, and
# left 71 adversarial teeth in `dregg-circuit-prove` alone reached by nothing — including
# `custom_binding_production_path`'s two forged-rejection poles, `fold_unfoolability_forge`,
# `accumulator::online_mixed_root_forgery_rejected`, `membership_binding_mechanism`'s forged
# pole, `recursion_vk_determinism`, and every one of the 28 in `circuit-prove/src/` (a
# `--test <binary>` list cannot name a LIB test at all, so no glob over `tests/*.rs` could
# ever have reached those, however it was spelled).
#
# ── FORMAT ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#     <route> <package> <test_fn>   # why
# One row per `#[ignore]`d test. The gate FAILS if a test has no row, if a row names a
# test that no longer exists, if an armed count falls below its floor, or if `unrouted`
# rises above its ceiling.
#
# ⚠ `unrouted` IS AN ALLOWED ANSWER AND IS THE HONEST ONE for a test nothing runs.
# Inventing a lane that does not run it is not. The count is a downward-only ratchet.
#
# ⚠ AND FOUR OTHER ROUTES ALSO MEAN "NOTHING RUNS IT" — `measurement`, `oversized`,
# `exclusive`, `fixture-mint`. They are more INFORMATIVE than `unrouted` (each says why a
# nightly cannot serve that test) and exactly as UNARMED. `gpu` likewise names a profile
# that needs an adapter, which no scheduled lane in this repository has. Only
# `armed-nightly`, `armed-dark` and `other-lane` name something that actually runs.
# 13 + 20 + 152 = 185 of the 282 are still executed by nothing; the ratchet is what stops
# that number growing while nobody is looking.
#
# ── WHAT THE CENSUS FOUND, BEYOND THE GLOB ───────────────────────────────────────────
# ⚑ Widening `binding-teeth` to the whole package would NOT have been right, and the
# tree's own `#[ignore]` reasons say why. `[profile.armed]` is
# `package(dregg-circuit-prove) and not (<six gpu names>)` at `test-threads = 4`, and
# sweeping it onto `ubuntu-latest` (4 vCPU / 16 GB) would have swept in:
#
#   * `oversized` — `leaf_wrap_mint_blowup_repricing::the_deployed_mint_is_the_measured_wall`
#     records "~118 GiB peak footprint (> RAM)", and `mina_accumulator_fold`'s three record
#     117.8–118.3 GiB. On a 16 GB runner that is an OOM, and an OOM reads as a failing tooth.
#   * `exclusive` — `production_leaves_mint_at_their_own_engine`'s two say "Run ALONE under
#     /usr/bin/time -l". At `test-threads = 4` they still produce a number; it is just wrong.
#   * `measurement` — probes with no adversarial claim. One says so in its own reason:
#     `dfa_routing_emit_gate::perf_prove_verify_breakdown` = "PERF PROBE with NO assertion".
#   * `fixture-mint` — tests whose effect is to WRITE a fixture into the tree.
#
# ⚑ AND FIVE GPU TESTS WERE IN NEITHER PROFILE (measured 2026-08-07; ⚑ REPAIRED 2026-08-08).
# `[profile.gpu]` named three binaries and six test names; `[profile.armed]`'s exclusion named
# the same six. These five were in neither list:
#     gpu_lde_parity_apex_scale_dim0_fold                          (circuit-prove/src/gpu_backend.rs)
#     deployed_arities_are_bit_exact_against_pinned_plonky3        (gpu_hidingfri_fold_differential)
#     lean_ir2_hidingfri_proof_uses_gpu_merkle_and_is_cpu_exact    (gpu_hidingfri_ir2_e2e)
#     required_hidingfri_refuses_disabled_gpu_merkle_stage         (gpu_hidingfri_ir2_e2e)
#     deployed_kernel_step_cpu_vs_gpu_across_fri_parameterizations (gpu_kernel_step_reparam_measure)
# `.config/nextest.toml`'s own doctrine already names this hazard — "a renamed GPU tooth
# drops out of `gpu` and into `armed`, i.e. onto GPU-less boxes, where it is the guaranteed
# red the GPU exclusion exists to prevent" — but these never ENTERED either list.
#
# ⚠ AND THE ROW BELOW USED TO SAY "the CPU nightly would red on them", WHICH IS NOT TRUE and
# is worth correcting rather than deleting, because it names the WRONG lane and so the wrong
# repair. Checked 2026-08-08 against what the scheduled lanes actually select: the nightly
# derives its targets from THIS roster (`--emit-cargo-targets`), and that emitter already
# `--skip`ped `gpu_lde_parity_apex_scale_dim0_fold` by name — it is a lib test, and `--lib`
# selects the whole lib target — while the other four live in binaries no armed route names,
# so nothing ever compiled them. The real exposure was `[profile.armed]`, i.e.
# `scripts/test-gauntlet.sh armed` on whatever box a human typed it on, which no schedule
# runs and which is exactly why nobody had seen the red.
#
# THE REPAIR, 2026-08-08: all five are now in `[profile.gpu]` and excluded from
# `[profile.armed]` (both edits in one commit — splitting them is how this recurs), and
# `scripts/test-gauntlet.sh gpu` exports `DREGG_REQUIRE_WGPU=1`, without which three of them
# assert-fail on line 1 of their own lane. They remain rostered `gpu` here, and `gpu` still
# means UNARMED: no scheduled lane in this repository has an adapter. What changed is that
# the lane which does have one now runs them, and no CPU lane can.
#
# ⚑ THIS ROSTER SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER A TOOTH BITES. The standing reminder is
# `armed-teeth.yml`'s own first measurement: arming the glob-covered set produced
# **4 passed / 11 FAILED of 17**. Routing is a precondition for biting, never evidence of it.
